subject: Operations runbook: metrics alignment for QBR prep
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Bethany Rogers <bethany@acmecloud.com>
Cc: ops-lead@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-08-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Operations runbook: metrics alignment for QBR prep

Team —

Attached is the monthly metrics dashboard (redwood_monthly_metrics_dashboard_v1.pdf) and a short read-ahead (qbr_read_prep.md). We need to close the following before the QBR packet goes to product & finance next Wednesday:

1) Ownership: confirm single owner for each metric (latency P50/P95, per-token cost, uptime, active usage by customer cohort).
2) Definitions: any divergence between metrics in the dashboard and the finance-backed definitions must be flagged.
3) Action items: owners should propose one mitigation or optimization per metric that is feasible within the quarter.

Quick asks:
- Markus, can you validate that the latency P95 in the dashboard excludes warm-start variance? If not, note the change and recommended replacement signal.
- Jasmine, please confirm the embedding inference cost normalization (per-embedding vs per-token equivalency) and add notes in the runbook.
- Laura, can you confirm uptime windows used for SLA backing and whether maintenance windows are excluded?
- Marissa, can you pull the top-5 customers by usage delta (MoM) and highlight any that require engagement before the QBR?

Bethany / AcmeCloud — thanks for the continued data sharing. If you have any corrections to the usage cohorts we pulled, please reply inline. We may ask for a short sync to reconcile a customer-level discrepancy.

I'm aiming to lock the final two slides (metrics + actions) by EOD Tuesday so the rest of the deck can be assembled on Wednesday. Please reply with owners / confirmations inline.

Irene
Irene Choi
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_monthly_metrics_dashboard_v1.pdf (PDF, 28 pages), qbr_read_prep.md (Markdown, 1.2 KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Bethany Rogers <bethany@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Operations runbook: metrics alignment for QBR prep

On 2026-08-18 16:12, Irene Choi wrote:
> Team —
>
> Attached is the monthly metrics dashboard ...

Thanks, Irene. Quick notes from my side:
- The P95 latency number currently in the dashboard mixes cold-start samples from the burst pool. I recommend switching to the "steady-state P95" we compute in the runtime traces (column: p95_steady_state) to avoid overcounting recent load tests. I'll mark that as my ownership and put a short note in the runbook link.
- For per-token cost, finance prefers amortized GPU-hour normalization for the QBR. I'll coordinate with finance and propose a reconciled per-token number by Tuesday noon.

Action: I own latency definition + per-token normalization alignment. I'll attach a one-page note to the Notion runbook by EOD Monday.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Bethany Rogers <bethany@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T21:37:00Z
Subject: Re: Operations runbook: metrics alignment for QBR prep

Thanks — tagging definitions here inline.

- Latency P50/P95: we should present both steady-state and end-to-end (including queue time) for the QBR. Steady-state shows runtime improvements; end-to-end is what customers see. I'll add a footnote to the dashboard.
- Per-token cost: redwood_monthly_metrics_dashboard_v1 uses per-token by inference-call weighting. For the QBR we will provide two columns: (a) per-token amortized (Markus will reconcile with finance) and (b) effective per-inference call median.
- Uptime: dashboard excludes scheduled maintenance windows >= 5 minutes by default; Laura, confirm whether we want to keep the 5-minute threshold or move to 1 minute to better reflect customer experience.
- Usage cohorts: Marissa — the cohort queries are on BigQuery (dataset: prod_metrics.cohorts) — I linked filters in the runbook.

I attached a short markdown with the metric glossary and my suggested slides.

Jasmine Liu
Head of Product Analytics
Redwood Inference

---
Attached: qbr_read_prep.md (contains metric glossary, slide outline, and suggested talking points)

From: Bethany Rogers <bethany@acmecloud.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Operations runbook: metrics alignment for QBR prep

Irene / team —

Thanks for the packet and clear asks. A couple of notes from AcmeCloud:
- Our usage cohort numbers match your cohort A/B split except for two customers (IDs 10234, 10987) where we attribute traffic to a different tenancy layer. I'll send a short CSV with reconciled IDs this afternoon.
- On uptime: for our contracts we treat any disruption > 30s as an incident; for QBR we prefer the 1-minute threshold Jasmine called out. That will better align with SLO reporting across our buyers.

We can do a 20-minute sync tomorrow PST if helpful to walk customer-level deltas; Bethany and our ops lead will join. If you only need the CSV and reconciliation notes, we'll send them into the HubSpot ticket (https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-4521) instead.

Best,
Bethany Rogers
Director, Customer Reliability
AcmeCloud
